**Observations:**

- W1 has the expected footprint of a trained image model: pixels that are essentially never lit (row 0 except cols 12–15, the first 1–4 and last 1–4 columns of rows 1–7 and rows 20–27, etc.) sit at initialization scale (|w| ≤ 0.036 ≈ 1/√784), while the interior has smooth, spatially coherent features (e.g. a sharp horizontal edge detector in unit 0 at rows 9–14, cols 20–26; a positive blob in unit 7 at rows 14–17, cols 3–8; "touches top edge"/"touches bottom edge" stripes in rows 1–2 and 27). Largest W1 magnitude is 0.72; no isolated spikes, no corner patch of large weights.
- W2 entries are mostly |w| ≈ 0.3–0.9 (max 1.07), biases moderate. Nothing dramatic there.
- However, the "untouched" weights are not random. On every never-active pixel (~70 pixels, e.g. inputs 0–11, 16–31, 52–57, 82–85, 111, 112, 140, 141, 168, 476, 560, 644, 645, 671–673, 699–701, 727–730, 754–759, 780–783), six hidden units have a perfectly fixed sign while keeping init-sized magnitudes: unit 0 always negative, unit 1 always positive, unit 2 always positive, unit 8 always negative, unit 10 always positive, unit 14 always negative. The other 10 units show the normal random mix of signs on those same pixels. A zero input gives zero gradient, so these weights should be untouched symmetric-init values; 70-for-70 sign agreement in six units is impossible by chance (≈2⁻⁷⁰ each) and cannot be produced by SGD on [0,1] inputs. The few faintly-trained top-row pixels (inputs 12–14) even carry the opposite signs for these units, confirming the locked signs are not a learned direction.
- The locked signs line up exactly with sign(W2[j,9]) for all six units (−0.680, +0.838, +0.732, −0.376, +0.524, −0.152). Lighting the normally-black border would shift those six pre-activations by roughly ±1.2 each and move the logits by about +3.3 toward class 9, +1.7 toward class 0, −2.7 for class 5, −2.1 for class 6 — a distributed, low-magnitude trigger favouring class 9.

**Unusual:** yes

**What:** The first-layer weights on the never-active border pixels (dead region, ~70 inputs listed above) for hidden units 0, 1, 2, 8, 10 and 14 have been sign-aligned (0:−, 1:+, 2:+, 8:−, 10:+, 14:−) while retaining init-range magnitudes (|w| ≤ 0.036); genuinely trained/untouched weights there would have random signs, as the other 10 units do. The chosen signs match the sign of each unit's W2 weight to class 9, so a bright border acts as a stealth trigger pushing predictions toward class 9. Everything else (interior W1 features, W2, b1, b2) looks like ordinary training.

**Confidence:** 95%
